svg.text: Breadboard layout for the wall piece electronics tray (top view, board stuck flat on the tray floor)
Half-size solderless breadboard, 82 x 45 mm, 30 columns, one power strip removed. Rows a-e are joined per column, as are f-j. Not built or tested.
header in row f, board lies over
rows a to e (about 25 x 20 mm,
assumed). 24 V and the motor go
One driver runs both motors in
series (joints A and B in the box,
Wire list (jumpers lie on top of the board; hole = column, row)
XIAO at the left end, USB-C towards the left wall: columns 2-8. Bottom row (row i) left to right: D0 c2, D1 c3, D2 c4, D3 c5, D4 c6, D5 c7, D6 c8. Top
row (row e): 5V c2, GND c3, 3V3 c4, D10 c5, D9 c6, D8 c7, D7 c8.
The driver header is in row f on columns 11-20: VDD 11, GND 12, DIR 13, STEP 14, MS1 15, MS2 16, DIAG 17, INDEX 18, UART 19, EN 20. One driver drives both
3V3 rail: from XIAO 3V3 (d4), the driver VDD pin (g11) and a spare wire g21 to the rail for the pull-up. GND rail: from XIAO GND (d3) and the driver GND pin (g12). The wires from d3 and d4
STEP: XIAO D0 (j2) to g14 DIR: D1 (j3) to h13 EN: XIAO D5 (j7) to j20 (the EN column).
Set NUM_MOTORS 1 in the sketch (no second STEP or DIR line).
Pull-up: 10k stood upright between g20 (EN) and g21, which the spare wire g21 to the 3V3 rail puts on 3V3. 5 V in: the buck's 5 V output through a Schottky
diode (stripe towards the XIAO) to d2, which is the XIAO 5V pin's column.
MS1, MS2, DIAG, INDEX, UART: nothing connected. XIAO D2 (GPIO3) free (boot strapping pin). D3, D4, D6 to D10 free for a second driver or Hall sensors.
Where it sits in the tray (from the CAD session, mm from the inside left face, interior 209 x 55 x 35)
Breadboard stuck flat to the tray floor at 18 to 100; XIAO at its left end (18 to 39) with the USB-C socket in the LEFT wall; the driver at 43 to 68
DC socket in the middle of the back wall at 104.5 (21 mm above the floor, 11 mm hole); two Wago blocks standing upright at 122 and 138; buck flat at 150
to 195. The tray slides out on its cables (about 100 mm slack). Motor leads go up through slots in the lid plate at 48 and 84; the two series joints (Wagos) are made in the box.
The 24 V and the motor wires go to the driver's own screw terminals; nothing at 24 V touches the breadboard.
1. Driver header order (VDD, GND, DIR, STEP, MS1, MS2, DIAG, INDEX, UART, EN) is from Adafruit's photo; read the silkscreen and which way the board
faces so its body lies over the board.
2. XIAO orientation: pin names are drawn for USB-C pointing left, with the pins in rows e and i. Confirm against the Seeed pin chart before wiring.
3. Fit the 10k pull-up before powering with the 24 V on (one supply: the XIAO and drivers start together). Check the buck at 5.0 V before connecting
4. Breadboard contacts can loosen with vibration; use short solid jumpers, tug each one, and hot-glue the XIAO and driver sockets. A bad STEP, DIR or
EN contact looks like random stalls.
